title: onboard-access-entropy-reduction-checklist-14d
short_summary: A pragmatic 14-day operational checklist and playbook focused on reducing access friction and configuration entropy during preboarding and first two weeks. Includes split ownership, email templates, gating rules, and rollback/escallation paths.
body:
Background:
Many recent joiner retros show time lost waiting for accounts, keys, and hardware. This doc frames a focused, repeatable 14-day sequence that reduces the number of handoffs where state drifts ("entropy") and creates clear owners and remediation steps when things stall.

Goals:
- Ensure >= 90% of new engineers have needed accounts and dev hardware within 48 hours of start.
- Reduce number of cross-team escalations for basic infra access by 70% compared to current baseline.
- Make preboard artifacts (access manifests, secrets, enrollment tickets) machine-checkable to lower manual verification.

Audience:
People Ops, IT/Hardware, SRE oncall, Hiring Managers, Team Leads, Facilities.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to engineers and technical ICs (software/platform/infra). Non-technical roles follow a lighter variant (see TODO links).
- Assumes hiring packet includes hardware tier decision at offer acceptance.
- Not a replacement for security approval flows; integrates with security gating.

High-level ownership model:
- People Ops (Primary): orchestrate preboard checklist, confirm offer-level hardware choice, and send preboard survey.
- IT/Hardware (Primary): provision laptop order, peripherals, asset tag, initial imaging.
- Infra Oncall / SRE (Secondary): sign off on cloud IAM pre-provisioning tickets and service account creation windows.
- Hiring Manager (Secondary): verify access list and priority repos/systems.

14-day checklist (practical steps, owners, SLAs):
Day -7 to -1 (Preboard window):
- People Ops: Send preboard survey (email template A) with hardware decision and personal laptop preferences. SLA: 72 hours for candidate response.
- People Ops: Create a single "Access Manifest" doc for the new hire listing exact repos, projects, groups, and 3rd-party tools. Attach to the new hire profile.
- IT: Receive order request, confirm shipping address, and trigger imaging ticket (SLA 48 hours).
- Infra: Create skeleton cloud principals/service accounts with temporary TTL (7 days) and mark as "pending-activation".

Day 0 (start date):
- People Ops: Send welcome packet and "Day 0 checklist" with links to Zoom, Slack invite, and self-serve troubleshooting.
- IT: Verify laptop delivery or pickup; if hardware delayed, escalate to People Ops and offer a vetted loaner (inventory pool).
- Hiring Manager: Join 1:1 and confirm high-priority access items; mark any exceptions.
- Infra: Activate cloud principals once IT confirms identity and asset tag.

Day 1–2:
- People Ops: Confirm Google/Okta and laptop login success via automated survey pings.
- IT: Complete endpoint hardening and MDM enrollment. Record serial and asset ID in the manifest.
- Infra: Grant access to core infra sandbox and 1 dev repo. Keep production-level permissions gated behind a 7-day trust window.
- Hiring Manager: Add the new hire to team-specific channels and invite to first sprint sync.

Day 3–5:
- People Ops: Run access audit against manifest; check granted vs requested. Any mismatches create an "access-fix" ticket with priority tag.
- Infra: Provision additional tooling keys (observability, deployment pipeline tokens) once the hiring manager confirms readiness.
- Mentor/Peer: Confirm dev environment build; if build fails, create a dedicated pairing slot within 48 hours.

Day 6–9:
- People Ops: Verify SSO sign-in to 3rd-party vendor services (Figma, Notion, CI). Revoke temporary tokens used for setup.
- IT: Confirm VPN / bastion access patterns; validate MFA is enforced.
- Infra: Run a permissions sweep and drop any accounts that remain in "pending-activation" beyond the TTL; open a corrective ticket to re-request if still needed.

Day 10–14:
- People Ops: Run a satisfaction pulse (short async survey) and a checklist reconciliation: everything in manifest must be either green / intentionally delayed / documented with owner.
- Hiring Manager: Complete first-week review; confirm readiness for broader repo and production access (if not, schedule canary ramp).
- People Ops: Close manifest, archive copies to the team folder, and log exceptions into hiring-retro board for continuous improvement.

Common failure modes and mitigation:
- Hardware delay: fallback pool policy (loaner + expedited shipping). People Ops triages and issues credit to candidate if shipping address error.
- IAM mismatch: automated manifest diff highlights gaps; Infra triages within 24 hours. If complexity high, apply temporary access with constrained TTL and full audit.
- Unresponsive hiring manager: People Ops escalates to manager's manager after 48 hours, with CC to eng leads.

Email templates (practical snippets):
- Preboard Survey invite (subject): "Quick preboard: hardware + access choices for <NAME>"
- Day 0 welcome (subject): "Welcome to Redwood — Day 0 checklist + fast help"
- Access escalation (subject): "URGENT: Missing access for <NAME> — action needed"

Gating rules and security notes:
- No production-level access before day 7 without explicit written exception from Security + Hiring Manager. Exceptions require documented risk acceptance.
- All service accounts created during preboard will have short TTLs and must be rotated or promoted after day 14.

Automation ideas (MVP backlog):
- Generate Access Manifest from offer form responses to avoid manual typing.
- Machine-verify Okta/G Suite group membership vs manifest and surface diffs daily.
- Auto-create one-click escalation workflow in Slack when manifest diff > threshold.

Rollbacks and emergency procedures:
- If a loaner device is lost/stolen, IT triggers remote wipe and flags asset in inventory. People Ops coordinates shipping replacement and notifies security.
- If a mistakenly-granted production access is detected, Infra issues immediate revocation and runs a permissions audit; People Ops notifies the hiring manager and Security.

Metrics and signals to track (recommended):
- Time-to-first-successful-login (median/90th)
- % of hires with full manifest green by day 3 and day 14
- Number of cross-team escalations per hire
- Loaner device utilization and stockouts

Next steps for pilots and rollouts:
1) Run a 20-hire pilot with two pods and baseline metrics for 6 weeks.
2) Build Access Manifest generator (MVP) and integrate with offer form.
3) Create a lightweight public dashboard for hiring managers showing manifest status.
4) Update security exception forms to require explicit TTLs and owner assignment.

Appendix — Quick links and troubleshooting cheatsheet:
- Who to ping: #new-joiner-ops (People Ops), #it-help (IT), #infra-oncall (SRE)
- Quick tickets: jira:HR-7121 (onboarding flow), jira:IT-3340 (hardware queue)
- Confluence: Onboarding Playbook (template), Security exception form

Notes to reviewers (things intentionally left rough):
- Need a lightweight variant for non-engineering hires (product, design) — will add after pilot.
- Hardware loaner policy needs legal signoff for international shipping.
- Consider adding a "buddy-pairing build checklist" to standardize environment builds.

Unresolved questions in the pilot:
- Threshold for auto-escalation: what % of manifest mismatch should trigger manager escalation?
- Who owns final decision for last-mile hardware substitutions when inventory low?
- Should we allow production access before day 7 for contractors under more aggressive NDAs?
next_steps: Run 20-hire pilot starting 2025-12-01 with two engineering pods
Prototype Access Manifest generator and connect to offer form
Create Slack automation for manifest diff alerts at 25% mismatch threshold
Draft loaner device international shipping legal addendum
unresolved_questions: Who has final signoff when hardware stock requires substitution?
Policy for contractor production access before day 7?
